author: EmuCore - Hub
title: PS2 vector unit demonstration Using only 16K of working space; NONE of the ps2 main CPU was used
summary: An archived SCEE Assembly 2002 programming-contest demonstration shows PS2 vector-unit code producing animated scenes in assembly within roughly 16 KB of working space, without relying on the main CPU for the featured workload.

blocks.text: The five-minute clip preserves a striking period demonstration rather than a modern explanation layered over emulator footage. According to the description, contest entries from an SCEE PS2 Linux seminar run in assembly with 16 KB or less of scratchpad memory and do not use the main CPU for the shown work. The animated puppet highlighted at 3:38 makes the constraint visible. It offers an intuitive example of why PS2 vector units were more than passive arithmetic helpers in ambitious specialist code.

The description is terse and does not identify which vector unit is used for every scene, how graphics output is submitted, what supporting setup occurs outside the measured space, or whether “no main CPU” excludes all initialization. The footage should therefore preserve the creator’s stated constraint rather than expand it into a complete architecture claim. Its value is as an archival capability demo. Detailed conclusions require the original seminar materials, contest rules and source code, none of which are linked here.
